questions.question: How does Python's GIL affect threading for CPU-bound tasks?
questions.expected_answer: Threads do not provide real speedup for CPU-bound work because only one thread executes Python bytecode at a time. Use multiprocessing for true parallelism.

questions.question: Is threading still useful for I/O-bound tasks in Python?
questions.expected_answer: Yes — the GIL is released during blocking I/O, so other threads can run.

questions.question: What is the GIL and why does it exist?
questions.expected_answer: The Global Interpreter Lock is a mutex that protects access to Python objects, simplifying memory management in CPython but limiting true multi-threaded execution.

questions.question: How does multiprocessing sidestep the GIL?
questions.expected_answer: Multiprocessing spawns separate processes that each have their own interpreter and memory space, so each can execute Python bytecode in parallel.

questions.question: What is asyncio and how does it relate to the GIL?
questions.expected_answer: asyncio is single-threaded cooperative concurrency; it sidesteps the GIL question entirely by running async I/O on a single event loop.

What chunking parameters are recommended for prose in RAG?
questions.expected_answer: Recursive character splitting with around 500-token chunks and ~80-token overlap.

questions.question: What does MMR balance in retrieval?
questions.expected_answer: Relevance to the query and diversity among the retrieved chunks.

questions.question: Why measure faithfulness, relevance, context precision, and hallucination separately?
questions.expected_answer: Each captures a distinct failure mode: faithfulness checks grounding, relevance checks the answer addresses the question, context precision checks retrieval quality, and hallucination checks for unsupported claims.

questions.question: Why use cosine similarity for sentence-transformer embeddings?
questions.expected_answer: Sentence-transformer models are trained with cosine-similarity objectives, so cosine is the natural distance metric for their outputs.

questions.question: What is the purpose of chunk overlap in recursive text splitting?
questions.expected_answer: Overlap preserves context across chunk boundaries so that a query whose answer straddles a split is still recoverable.

questions.question: Why is local embedding preferable to a hosted API for RAG prototyping?
questions.expected_answer: It removes API cost, latency, and rate-limit constraints, and avoids leaking documents to a third party during development.

questions.question: What does context precision measure and how is it scored?
questions.expected_answer: It measures whether the retrieved chunks are actually relevant to the question; an LLM-as-judge classifies each chunk as relevant or not.

questions.question: When does threading speed up CPU-bound Python code?
questions.expected_answer: It generally does not — for CPU-bound work, threads compete for the GIL and provide no real speedup. Multiprocessing is the standard alternative.

questions.question: What is the trade-off when increasing the chunk size?
questions.expected_answer: Larger chunks preserve more context per retrieval but reduce recall precision and may push out genuinely relevant content from the top-k window.
